output.brief: The evidence doesn't point to RotaWeave alone, and cancelling it is unlikely to fix the problem. The drop comes from two changes landing together at Dock Street and Westgate. Those sites went onto the app on 14 April and lost their coordinators on 1 May. The basic app tier has no recurring bookings, so a regular only keeps a weekly slot if staff book it before Thursday's release. Staff bookings there fell from 74 a week to 3 a week after 1 May. Of 213 April regulars at those two sites, 129 lost their usual slot at least twice, and 88% of them are now inactive. Only 11% of those who kept their slot left. Two comparison sites show neither change is enough alone. Millbrook has the app and a coordinator, and its numbers are flat. Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but has no app and a lead volunteer keeping the paper roster, and its numbers are flat too. Background checks don't explain it. 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current check, and 21 of the 23 deactivated on 1 May came back. Commonplate was named in only 2 of the 61 callbacks. Next steps: do not cancel the app, suspend checks, or purge the roster. Have staff or trained leads book regulars into their usual slots before each Thursday release, phone lapsed regulars to offer their slot back, and review after 60 days. Also resolve whether the board gets the Quarry Lane go-live on 6 October without that fix. My confidence is fairly high but rests on one site-level extract and one staff-compiled reconciliation.
